bio_en: Satenik Matinian, known by the party name Tsaghik and later as Satenik Arghutian, was born in Alexandropol into the Matinian family; her brother Nikol and sister Natalia were also among the founding forces of the ARF, and in the late 1880s the family home in Tiflis was a meeting place of the party's founders. She left the sixth class of the Tiflis gymnasium for revolutionary work and in 1892 went to Tabriz as a teacher with a group that included Hovnan, Duman, Ishkhan (Yervand-Dasho), Toros and Sako. Teaching was a cover: she became one of the leading revolutionary figures in Persia, organising women's and student groups in Tabriz and carrying arms to Salmast, Khoy, the Derik monastery and Kars. She became the life companion of Hovsep Arghutian (Ishkhan) and died in Paris on 12 December 1930 after a long illness; the two are buried together in Chaville.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Earlier text (#531) describes the Tiflis family home; #659 gives Alexandropol as her origin.
